about: Stage B2 of the A02 complete-activity package (12 November 2026), on Christian's reply received 12 November 2026, items 1, 2, 5 and 6. Each entry in the approved table's cover shape says, in one sentence, the fields of a condition only approved words may say (register rows V4-V6), matched to the exact values the realized A02-HPE1 game holds (our CANDIDATE restatement of RPC-002 in rpc-002-contract.DRAFT.json, the escape line PROPOSED in a02-proposed/hpe1.PROPOSED.json); a value that drifts no longer matches, the field is withheld and the build refuses (fail closed). In place of approvedBy, each carries candidateBy: ours, dated, the approved rows it restates (verbatim at their line of the RPC library) and Christian's words it rests on (verbatim in the rulings recorded in back/src/system/design-reasoning/a02-inputs.review.json, with the received date). The printed-only sentences are never said by the engine: the review print shows them beside the served text, in their part and with their label (PROPOSED: new knowledge of ours, for Christian's approval; CANDIDATE: our wording of approved knowledge). Kept out of every sentence, visible for ecological review: the immediate-shot incentive (A02-12NOV-NEXT-ACTION, word 14). Since stage A2 (13 November 2026, the lead's decision W1) the coach text: our sentences take the base of round 1's rewrite; the condition sentence says 'possession', never 'attack', and nothing that presupposes the escape succeeded; a sentence of ours may state one or more of the engine's sentences in fewer words (`standsFor`, each engine sentence by its exact text), and the review print (four-part-print.unit.ts) prints it in their place, takes their grades and requires each engine sentence printed exactly once; a printed sentence resting on a PROPOSED element it does not state names the question (`restsOn`). The optional restart sentence (S6) is merged into the PROPOSED restart's line (R1), and the event-completion sentence (K3's first) is gone. FIX (13 November 2026, from the V3 and V4 verifications): 'before scoring' for 'before it scored' (the 'it' could be read as the pressing team); 'passes or forward options', as Christian's 'or'; the stoppage sentence no longer repeats the next action, and says 'judgment'; the pressing team's sentence says 'a point', as the escaping team's does; the learning explanation names the condition in the scoring line's words; each printed sentence names every question it rests on (restsOn), the escaping team's noun (Q1) included, so a print that states none of the engine's sentences still shows its grades; the placement rule carries its own ILLUSTRATIVE label (illustrative); R1's support no longer cites the sentence that leaves the starting arrangement to the coach, which cuts the other way (it is put beside question Q6 instead).

match.equals: retains possession through the next action

entries.sentence: The escaping team scores a point when a player dribbles over the line, or receives and controls the ball beyond it, and the team keeps the ball through its next action. It counts only if, in that possession, the escaping team faced the pressing team pressing together before scoring: players working together to pressure the ball and restrict passes or forward options. One player closing down alone does not necessarily count. A player who dribbles over the line and keeps the ball needs no extra touch. No point if play stops first; use your judgment for unusual stoppages.
standsFor: Escaping team: Score by getting the ball under control into its target zone: running it in, or passing to a teammate who receives it under control inside
Mark the escaping team's target zone from the marked line to the pressing team's end line, across the full width

restates.words: The sequence begins under established coordinated pressure, the event occurs beyond the pressing line, and the attacking team retains possession through the next action.

rulings.quote: A qualifying sequence begins when the attacking team possesses the ball while facing established, coordinated defensive pressure.
That means defenders are working in connection with one another to pressure the ball and restrict relevant passing or progression opportunities.
An isolated defender closing down the ball does not necessarily constitute coordinated pressure.
The pressure condition applies at the beginning of the qualifying sequence, not continuously throughout its entirety.
A scoring event must occur within a sequence that began under coordinated pressure.
We shouldn't require the press to remain intact after it has been broken.
Whose action: The attacking team's next relevant ball action following completion of the scoring event.
The approved condition should recognize a successful continuation of attacking possession following the qualifying advancement event, without prescribing the type of action.
Successful continuation: The attacking team must retain possession through the continuation.
If play stops first: Ordinarily the continuation requirement has not been completed, so the point has not yet been earned.
Practical exceptions involving unusual stoppages should remain subject to reasonable coach judgment rather than an elaborate universal rule.
For a player already carrying or dribbling, please avoid introducing an artificial extra touch, distance or time requirement simply to create a separate action.
The coach should not have to interpret those technical distinctions or read several paragraphs to understand the game.
